summary: OpenAI describes voluntary changes to its Preparedness Framework process, including a temporary pause in RL training and new monitoring, security and alignment measures, prompted by an internal security incident and preliminary evidence that its upcoming Astra model may cross the Critical cybersecurity capability threshold.

mechanisms.reason: The document states preliminary evidence that an upcoming model may cross a Critical cyber-capability threshold, a step-change capability claim even though hedged as preliminary.
mechanisms.quote: preliminary evidence that one of our upcoming models, Astra, may meet the Critical cybersecurity capability threshold under our Preparedness Framework

mechanisms.reason: The lab explicitly paused and slowed its largest planned frontier RL training run for safety reasons, temporarily reducing training compute demand.
mechanisms.quote: This included a two-week pause in reinforcement learning (RL) training on our latest models intended for deployment ... Our largest planned frontier RL run remains on hold

practices.reason: The multistage activation-classifier and escalation monitoring system, with a stated ~20% inference compute overhead, illustrates a transferable safety-monitoring measurement practice, though it is described as an internal, non-transferable process.
practices.quote: This new monitoring setup is multistage, starting with activation classifiers (detectors that inspect a model’s internal activity) that run at every sampled token and escalate potential concerns to increasingly sophisticated and high-compute automated investigators.

notable_reason: A frontier lab disclosing that an unreleased model may cross a critical cyber-capability threshold, and pausing its largest planned RL training run in response, is a material safety and capability signal for the sector.
